newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal Sud FM radio on air again after brief ban.
newsitem.headline: Senegal Sud FM radio on air again after brief ban.

text.p: Senegal's private Sud FM radio station was back on the air on Friday after paying a broadcasting fee demanded by the government.
Senegal stopped three private stations from broadcasting on August 9 because they had not paid the fee to the state radio station, as required under their licence.
"We have paid our broadcasting fees, although we found it unfair to pay the fee to our competitor," Cherif Elvalid Seye, the manager of SUD FM, told Reuters.
"Where else in the world do you compete with someone and also have to pay them a fee?" he said.
Senegal's Communications Minister Serigne Diop banned Sud FM, Nostalgie and Dunya for three months.
Sud FM has now paid its 20 million CFA francs ($32,000), and Diop told state television that a solution would soon be found as regards the other two stations.
